description: Three specs independently deferred the SAME single-authority to federation question, each promising to 'likely resolve the same way': KINP §11 decision 1 (a single canonical identity authority ROLE for real-world entities; 'federation stays a future option', identity.md around line 477), KCB §7 open question 1 (a single host-provisioned registry vs per-org registries that peer; 'Mirrors KINP §11 decision 1', capability-bus.md ~line 251), and KMI §9 open question 3 (single shared CAS vs per-project stores that replicate on reference; 'mirrors KINP §11 authority fork and KCB §7 registry federation', media-interchange.md ~line 380). This tasklist resolves that shared single-authority-role to federated-peers pattern ONCE, in a new agnostic ADR, so the three specs stop deferring it three separate ways (ROADMAP.md Phase F1). PARKED: per the roadmap, nothing is built until a real deployment actually needs more than one authority; this file is the authored proposal, held until that trigger. Public-safe/agnostic per decisions/README.md: bind roles, standards named only as adopted standards, number at or above 0009 (0002-0004 permanently reserved; 0005-0008 taken).

userStories.title: ADR resolving the shared single-authority-role to federated-peers pattern once
userStories.description: Write one agnostic ADR that resolves the pattern the three specs each defer to — a single authority as a ROLE today, federation as the future option — so KINP/KCB/KMI can point at one decision instead of restating it.
acceptanceCriteria: A new decisions/ADR (numbered at or above 0009; 0002-0004 reserved, 0005-0008 taken) records the shared decision: the pattern by which a single authority ROLE (identity authority, discovery registry, CAS) generalizes to federated peers, stated once so KINP §11 decision 1, KCB §7 open question 1, and KMI §9 open question 3 all cite it.

The ADR presents the fork fairly before deciding — single privileged authority role vs fully federated peers with no privileged node — and preserves the invariant the three specs already share: authority is a role, not a hard dependency, and offline-first minting must not require reaching the authority (KINP §11, §6).

The ADR is agnostic per decisions/README.md (binds roles; names no deployment, topology, or product except as illustrative/known-implementation pointers), and decisions/README.md's records table gains a row for it.

The ADR names the concrete cross-authority hazards a later pressure test must hunt (cross-authority same_as reconciliation, registry peering, per-project CAS replication on reference) without specifying a deployment — it resolves contract SHAPE only.

userStories.title: Record the ADR as the single referent for the three deferred questions
userStories.description: Make the ADR the durable single source the three open questions defer to, without yet editing the normative clauses (that is tasklist 52, gated on this ADR).
acceptanceCriteria: The ADR explicitly enumerates the three deferral sites it supersedes (KINP §11 decision 1, KCB §7 open question 1, KMI §9 open question 3) and states that the per-spec §-edits applying it are the follow-up (chief/52-federation-spec-edits) and the multi-authority pressure test is chief/53-multi-authority-scenario.
No normative spec clause is edited in THIS tasklist (the §-edits are 52); this story only lands the ADR and its README row, so no spec version is bumped here.
The ADR records what stays invariant regardless of when federation is switched on, so the future §-edits are additive rather than a breaking redefinition.
